key_idea: By recasting tiling constraints as a functional programming language, one can 'program' a 2-adically structured Sudoku puzzle that forces aperiodicity, which is then compiled down into a single tiling equation.
reason: Treating a single tile equation as a programmable logic system that can enforce an aperiodic Sudoku grid is a deeply surprising and conceptually brilliant cross-field insight. While this yields a highly elegant core mechanism, mechanically compiling the logical constraints into a single tile demands an intricate, massive hierarchy of lemmas and dense bookkeeping.
recognized: Greenfeld and Tao, A counterexample to the periodic tiling conjecture
